label: No Great Depression Occurred
detail: The 1929 crash passes without a lasting slump, so 1932 is an ordinary year of work, wages and steady farm and bank conditions.
assumption: Economic distress is removed as a driver of the vote, so voters judge the party in office on peacetime prosperity and on non-economic issues such as Prohibition, rather than on the slump.
facts_text: Business has stayed steady since 1929, and factories, farms and banks are working at ordinary levels.
Few men are out of work, and bread lines and relief appeals are not part of the news.
Prices for wheat and cotton have held near their late-1920s levels, and bank failures have been rare.
research_questions: How did voters in 1920 and 1928 behave when times were good and the party in office sought another term?
How did voters in different regions and groups shift between 1928 and 1932 as unemployment and farm prices worsened?
Did the Prohibition issue weigh more heavily on voters in years of prosperity, such as 1924 and 1928?
source_text: what if the great depression never happened?
